subject: general
question:
Choose the correct option to give a one-word substitution for the sentence given.
A person who can talk non-stop or can speak continuously.
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Garrulous .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Garrulous** refers to a person who talks a lot, often excessively or in a verbose manner.
 
• The other options provided do not match the meaning of the sentence:
 
 
• **Precipitous:** Refers to something steep or sudden, not related to speech.
 
• **Circumvent:** Means to avoid or bypass, not related to talking.
 
• **Sparkling:** Refers to something bright or shining, unrelated to speech.
 
 
• Hence, option 1 (**Garrulous**) is the correct one-word substitution for a person who talks non-stop or continuously.

Correct sentence: *A person who can talk non-stop is **Garrulous**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One-word substitutions are used to express lengthy sentences or phrases in a concise manner.
 
• Examples of similar one-word substitutions:
 
 
• **Loquacious:** Another word for someone who talks a lot.
 
• **Taciturn:** The opposite of garrulous; refers to someone who speaks very little.
